stories.headline: NBA Rank 2026, players Nos. 50-11: Where LeBron, Steph, KD check in
stories.summary: Our countdown of the NBA's top 100 players continues. See which stars just missed a spot in the top 10 -- and where three legends land.
stories.body:
NBA Rank is back! With less than one month until opening night, let's continue counting down the league's best players for 2026-27.

After unveiling players Nos. 100-51 on Tuesday, our rankings now enter the top 50. It's a group headlined by former MVPs, future first-ballot Hall of Famers and young stars expected to take major leaps this season.

It's also where LeBron James checks in, his first time outside the top 10 in NBA Rank's 15-year history. (You can jump to LeBron's NBA Rank here.)

The rankings rollout concludes Thursday with our expert panel's top 10 players. And that panel has been overhauled for the 2026 edition.

In previous seasons, more than 100 ESPN NBA insiders, reporters, editors and producers voted on thousands of possible player vs. player matchups to arrive at the final top-100 list. That "wisdom of the crowd" approach has given way to the wisdom of seven: ESPN's Ben Golliver, Vincent Goodwill, Zach Kram, Bobby Marks, Dave McMenamin, André Snellings and Matt "Stats" Williams. (The panelists' individual top-100 lists were combined to create our final rankings.)

Voting guidelines, however, remained unchanged. The panel was asked to rank players based on predicted contributions -- quality and quantity -- for the 2026-27 regular season only.

Let's get to the list, which features plenty of superstars who just missed our top 10.

Note: Signature stats provided by ESPN Research.

50. Dylan Harper
G | San Antonio Spurs

Age: 20

2025 NBA Rank: NR

The youngest member of the Spurs was the one who seemed to rise highest in the altitude of the Finals and stands to make a big jump in Year 2, whether he stays coming off the bench or makes the leap to the first five. He will earn more respect from the officials (1.7 free throw attempts in 69 games as a rookie), take a bigger role in the offense and improve on his already-respectable playmaking. Harper is an All-Star in the making. -- Vincent Goodwill

Signature stat: Harper had six games with at least 15 points and 65% shooting from the field in the 2026 playoffs, the most by a guard in NBA postseason history.

Fantasy projection: 15.2 PTS, 5.0 AST, 4.4 REB

49. Lauri Markkanen
F | Utah Jazz

Age: 29

2025 NBA Rank: 43

Markkanen, a scoring forward who can stretch the court, has languished as a forgotten man in Utah. The Finnish star's competence often came into conflict with the Jazz's desire to improve their draft positioning during a multiyear rebuilding effort, and he has appeared in only one game in April over the past four seasons. Though his contract is overly generous for a player lacking All-NBA credentials, Markkanen should benefit from Utah's recent talent upgrades as he eyes his first career postseason appearance. -- Ben Golliver

Signature stat: Markkanen has nine seasons with at least 100 3-pointers, tied with Karl-Anthony Towns and Dirk Nowitzki for the most by a 7-footer in NBA history.

Fantasy projection: 23.8 PTS, 7.2 REB, 1.9 AST

48. Kon Knueppel
G | Charlotte Hornets

Age: 21

2025 NBA Rank: NR

Knueppel had a historic debut season. He finished second for Rookie of the Year behind a rookie-record, Hornets-record and NBA season-high 273 made 3-pointers. There will be change for Knueppel this upcoming season, as LaMelo Ball and Miles Bridges are both gone. Ball assisted on 73 of Knueppel's 3s last season, the fourth most by any passer-scorer combination. Bridges assisted on 49, the second most on the team. -- Matt Williams

Signature stat: Knueppel was the first rookie to lead the NBA in made 3-pointers (272). Prior to last season, no first-year player had ever finished in the top three.

Fantasy projection: 20.0 PTS, 5.8 REB, 3.7 AST

47. Derrick White
G | Boston Celtics

Age: 32

2025 NBA Rank: 26

An inconsistent season on offense has White sliding back twenty-one spots. White continues to be one of the league's best defenders but an inconsistent season on offense has him sliding back 21 spots. For the first time in his career, White shot less than 40% from the field. In the playoffs, White's points per game decreased from 16.5 in the regular season to 8.7 in the first round. He shot 30.9% from the field and 26.5% on 3s. With Jaylen Brown traded to Philadelphia, the Celtics need consistency from White to contend in the revamped Eastern Conference. White has three years and $98 million remaining on his contract. -- Bobby Marks

Signature stat: Among qualified players, White saw the largest drop in effective field goal percentage from 2024-25 to 2025-26.

Fantasy projection: 16.6 PTS, 5.3 AST, 1.2 BLK

46. Brandon Miller
F | Charlotte Hornets

Age: 23

2025 NBA Rank: 76

Charlotte's deals with Minnesota (LaMelo Ball) and Phoenix (Miles Bridges) weren't just signals of a change in the franchise's direction, but they were a tacit endorsement of Miller. Selected No. 2 in 2023, the 6-7 forward is a proven scorer (19.0 points per game for his career) and made strides in his efficiency last season by setting personal bests in accuracy from 3 (38.3%) and the foul line (89.2%). -- Dave McMenamin

Signature stat: Despite the presence of Ball and the emergence of Knueppel, it was Miller who led Charlotte with 20.2 points per game last season.

Fantasy projection: 22.3 PTS, 5.4 REB, 3.7 AST

45. Franz Wagner
F | Orlando Magic

Age: 25

2025 NBA Rank: 32

Wagner is a talented shooter-scorer on the wing whose 6-10 size makes him a nightly mismatch. The main thing standing between Wagner and his first All-Star selection has been health, with him playing only 94 of a possible 162 games the past two seasons. But Wagner has averaged 22.9 points per game in that span and matches with Paolo Banchero and Desmond Bane to give the Magic one of the most formidable 2-3-4 combos in the NBA. -- André Snellings

Signature stat: Orlando went 20-14 in Wagner's career-low 34 games played last season (25-23 without).

Fantasy projection: 22.5 PTS, 5.7 REB. 4.2 AST

44. Trae Young
G | Washington Wizards

Age: 28

2025 NBA Rank: 29

Other than finagling his way to a new four-year, $212.8 million contract -- a huge win, to be fair -- the past year was one to forget for Young. He played only 15 games due to injuries and was traded to the team with the worst record in the league. Meanwhile, the Hawks took off in the standings after dealing him.

In his first full season as a Wizard, Young will surely do his part to boost an offense that ranked 29th in efficiency last year, but he won't help a defense that ranked 30th. One major question for Washington is how much Young dominates on the ball, versus occasionally spacing the floor and deferring to the Wizards' young playmakers on the perimeter. -- Kram

Signature stat: Young, Oscar Robertson, LeBron James and Nikola Jokic are the only players in NBA history with at least 25 points and 10 assists per game in consecutive seasons.

Fantasy projection: 23.8 PTS, 10.8 AST, 1.2 STL

43. De'Aaron Fox
G | San Antonio Spurs

Age: 28

2025 NBA Rank: 35

Fox smoothly downshifted into his new life as Wembanyama's sidekick in their first full season together, but the 6-foot-3 guard's poor play in the Finals led critics to call for him to be benched or traded. San Antonio stood by Fox this summer, opting to keep the two-time All-Star and the bulk of its 62-win team intact. However, the scrutiny on Fox will only intensify with 2025 lottery pick Dylan Harper eyeing an expanded role. Fox's unsightly 41/29/76 shooting splits in the 2026 playoffs simply must improve for the Spurs to fulfill their championship dreams. -- Golliver

Signature stat: Fox ranks fourth in clutch time points since entering the league in 2017-18, behind DeMar DeRozan, LeBron James and Nikola Jokic.

Fantasy projection: 20.6 PTS, 5.6 AST, 1.4 STL

42. Rudy Gobert
C | Minnesota Timberwolves

Age: 34

2025 NBA Rank: 49

The Timberwolves ranked eighth in defensive efficiency last season, but their success varied depending on the presence of Gobert. When he was on the floor, they had a 108.0 defensive rating. That rose to 115.9 when Gobert was on the bench. But the intriguing part of Gobert's game this season will be his partnership with LaMelo Ball in the pick-and-roll. Ball ranked second in on-ball screens as the ball handler last season, while Gobert was third in picks set as the screener, according to GeniusIQ player tracking. -- Williams

Signature stat: Gobert's four Defensive Player of the Year awards are tied for the most in NBA history with Dikembe Mutombo and Ben Wallace.

Fantasy projection: 11.9 PTS, 11.7 REB, 1.7 BLK

41. Joel Embiid
C | Philadelphia 76ers

Age: 32

2025 NBA Rank: 47

When Embiid plays, he's productive and must be accounted for on every scouting report -- a shoo-in for 27 points and eight boards and a matchup nightmare with his ability to score at all three levels. But "when he plays" is still an issue, the biggest question mark for whether this talent-laden 76ers experiment can lead to a run through May. Since winning MVP in 2023, he has played in a possible 96 of 246 games (39%). -- Goodwill

Signature stat: Embiid has averaged 27.64 points per game throughout his career, fourth most in NBA history and second most by a frontcourt player (Wilt Chamberlain: 30.07).

Fantasy projection: 27.4 PTS, 8.2 REB, 1.2 BLK

40. Anthony Davis
F | Washington Wizards

Age: 33

2025 NBA Rank: 14

It has been a disastrous couple of seasons for Davis since his shocking trade from the Lakers to the Mavericks. He has appeared in just 29 games since late-January 2025 and was traded a second time to the Wizards in February. Davis has yet to play for Washington due to a hand injury but enters 2026-27 fully healthy, and his on-court performance this season will be key to his long-term future after Davis' representatives and the Wizards shelved extension talks this summer. He's owed $58.5 million this season and has a $62.8 million player option for 2027-28. -- McMenamin

Signature stat: Davis is one of 11 players to average 20 points and 10 rebounds per game in at least 10 seasons. The only other player among the 11 to have played in the 21st century is Shaquille O'Neal, with a league-record 13 20-10 seasons.

Fantasy projection: 22.6 PTS, 11.4 REB, 2.1 BLK

39. Kyrie Irving
G | Dallas Mavericks

Age: 34

2025 NBA Rank: NR (injury)

Irving was 25th two years ago but dropped out of the top 100 while recovering from a torn right ACL. The 34-year-old has averaged at least 20 points per game in nine straight seasons and rejoins a revamped Maverick roster featuring Cooper Flagg and new coach Dusty May. A healthy Irving will improve an offense that ranked 22nd in assists and 29th in 3-pointers made. Irving has two years left on his contract, including a player option in 2027-28, and could be a trade candidate if Dallas is out of playoff contention by February. -- Marks

Signature stat: Irving, who has routinely flirted with shooting splits of 50% from the field, 40% from 3 and 90% from the free throw line, pulled off the feat in 2020-21. He is one of three players in NBA history with a 50/40/90 season on at least 20 shots per game (Stephen Curry in 2015-16, Larry Bird in 1986-87 and 1987-88).

Fantasy projection: 24.6 PTS, 4.8 AST, 1.3 STL

38. Stephon Castle
G | San Antonio Spurs

Age: 21

2025 NBA Rank: 99

Castle raised his game in every way as a sophomore. He was a dominant defender coming out of college, with the size and strength of a big wing but with the quickness and tenacity to lock up opposing point guards. Castle's offensive game is developing as he improves as both a shooter and a distributor, both skills building from his natural ability to get to the rim off the dribble. Castle joins Wembanyama and Harper as the young, supremely talented nucleus of a Spurs team that seems destined for many more Finals trips. -- Snellings

Signature stat: Last season, Castle became the youngest player in NBA history to record at least 40 points, 12 rebounds, and 12 assists in a game.

Fantasy projection: 18.1 PTS, 7.6 AST, 5.6 REB

37. Austin Reaves
G | Los Angeles Lakers

Age: 28

2025 NBA Rank: 60

Reaves' dream season was cut short in April by an oblique injury that, paired with Luka Doncic's hamstring strain, helped derail the Lakers' postseason. He was still rewarded with a four-year, $180 million extension to stay in L.A. and build the next era with Doncic after LeBron James' departure to the 76ers in free agency. The 6-5 combo guard has shown his ability to make plays for himself and others at a high level. The next step in him reaching All-Star status will be his continued improvement defensively and having health on his side like in 2023-24 when he played all 82 games. -- McMenamin

Signature stat: Reaves is one of two undrafted players to sign a $100 million NBA contract, along with fellow Wichita State alum Fred VanVleet.

Fantasy projection: 23.4 PTS, 5.9 AST, 4.9 REB

36. Paolo Banchero
F | Orlando Magic

Age: 23

2025 NBA Rank: 17

Banchero is an imposing forward whose stock has taken a slight hit due to his inability to smooth out his rough edges. While the 2022 No. 1 overall pick has regularly stuffed the stat sheet and led the Magic to three straight playoff appearances, he has also collected naysayers who decry his anachronistic shot selection and choppy decision-making. Banchero ranked 33rd in true shooting percentage out of the 42 players who attempted at least 1,000 shots last season, and the Magic have never ranked higher than 18th in offensive efficiency during his career. -- Golliver

Signature stat: Last season, Banchero joined Luka Doncic as the only players to score at least 35 points in their first two career Game 7s.

Fantasy projection: 23.4 PTS, 7.9 REB, 5.2 AST

35. LaMelo Ball
G | Minnesota Timberwolves

Age: 25

2025 NBA Rank: 63

The Timberwolves needed a point guard and additional creator next to Anthony Edwards and they got that in Ball. Health had been an issue over the past few seasons, but Ball played 72 games in 2025-26, his most since 2021-22 (75). And despite a career low in minutes, Ball ranked second in made 3-pointers and was one of eight players to average 20 points and seven assists per game. -- Williams

Signature stat: Ball averages 3.22 made 3-pointers per game for his career, the second most in NBA history among players with at least 300 games played. (Stephen Curry's 3.97 per game is first.)

Fantasy projection: 23.1 PTS, 8.0 AST, 5.4 REB

34. OG Anunoby
F | New York Knicks

Age: 29

2025 NBA Rank: 41

It all came together for Anunoby last postseason. One of the league's most consistent players, despite never making an All-Star team, stepped into the forefront. That tip-in in Game 4 of the Finals was one of the biggest baskets in Madison Square Garden history, and he'll be royalty forever for it. Quietly, though, he might've been the Knicks' second-best player in the postseason (20.1 points on ridiculous 56/49/85 splits) while still playing lockdown defense. He'll be tasked with guarding wings and bigs as the Knicks try to repeat. -- Goodwill

Signature stat: Anunoby joined Walt Frazier and Bernard King as only Knicks players to average at least 20 points, five rebounds and 55% shooting in the postseason.

Fantasy projection: 16.9 PTS, 5.2 REB, 1.5 STL

33. Jalen Duren
C | Detroit Pistons (restricted FA)

Age: 22

2025 NBA Rank: NR

An All-NBA season puts Duren in the top 35 for the first time, but questions remain despite last year's regular-season success. First, will the contract stalemate end before the start of training camp or will Duren play out this season on a one-year, $9.6 million qualifying offer? The deadline to sign the offer is Oct. 1. Second, will Duren's postseason struggles carry over? In the 2026 playoffs, Duren averaged 10.1 points per game, the second-largest scoring decrease from the regular season to the postseason in NBA history, according to ESPN Research. -- Marks

Signature stat: Last season, Duren became the first Piston to average at least 15 points, 10 rebounds and 60% shooting from the field.

Fantasy projection: 20.3 PTS, 11.7 REB, 1.0 BLK

32. James Harden
G | Cleveland Cavaliers

Age: 37

2025 NBA Rank: 23

In many ways, Harden remains the same player now, in his late 30s, as he was half a decade ago, or even to some extent in his prime. He always orchestrates efficient offenses. He takes (and makes) smart shots and still generates gobs of free throws. And he's an indifferent defender at the best of times.

After a midseason trade to Cleveland, Harden meshed well with Donovan Mitchell, as the Cavaliers posted a 126.4 offensive rating with that duo on the floor, per databallr. Cleveland is hoping for more of the same, or an even better performance, in their first full season together. -- Kram

Signature stat: Harden has seven seasons with at least 20 points and 8 assists per game, tied with Oscar Robertson (10) for second all-time.

Fantasy projection: 20.6 PTS, 8.1 AST, 5.0 REB

31. Amen Thompson
F | Houston Rockets

Age: 23

2025 NBA Rank: 37

At 6-7 with a sturdy frame and explosive leaping ability, Thompson profiled as a prototypical 3-and-D wing. But his offensive game has developed rapidly in each of his three seasons, allowing him to play a lot of point forward with his ability to penetrate off the dribble and break down opposing defenses with an eye for playmaking. Thompson is the basketball equivalent of a five-tool prospect who is growing into a franchise centerpiece. -- Snellings

Signature stat: Thompson and Cleveland's Evan Mobley were the only players with at least 200 dunks last season. Thompson's 201 dunks were the most by a player shorter than 6-10 since Montrezl Harrell in 2018-19 (203).

Fantasy projection: 17.7 PTS, 7.7 REB, 5.1 AST, 1.5 STL

30. Alperen Sengun
C | Houston Rockets

Age: 24

2025 NBA Rank: 25

In Houston's first game last season, Sengun made a career-high five 3-pointers against the Thunder; it seemed as if he was poised to take a leap. But the rest of the season didn't quite work out that way, as Sengun finished with essentially the same numbers as he has in every recent season. For instance, his player efficiency rating has been 22.0, 21.4 and 21.4 over the past three years.

Those numbers are still sufficient to make Sengun an All-Star, but not the primary option on a contender. Combine that offensive plateau with a minor step back defensively, and Sengun's ceiling looks lower now than it did a year ago. -- Kram

Signature stat: Sengun, Oscar Robertson and Luka Doncic are the only players in NBA history to average 20 points, eight rebounds and five assists in multiple seasons before turning 24 years old.

Fantasy projection: 20.0 PTS, 9.4 REB, 5.7 AST

29. Pascal Siakam
F | Indiana Pacers

Age: 32

2025 NBA Rank: 22

Siakam was the lone bright spot in a miserable Pacers season following Tyrese Haliburton's injury in the 2025 NBA Finals. He made the All-Star team and put up the second-highest scoring average in his career on higher volume. This season, Haliburton returns and Siakam returns to his role as co-star on a team that has designs on getting back to the NBA Finals. At 32 years old, his game should still be highly effective, and at times he can be a potent scorer (14 games of 30 points or more). -- Goodwill

Signature stat: Siakam is one of three players with at least 2,000 minutes and 1,000 points in each of the past eight seasons (DeMar DeRozan, Nikola Jokic).

Fantasy projection: 22.8 PTS, 7.3 REB, 4.0 AST

28. Bam Adebayo
C | Miami Heat

Age: 29

2025 NBA Rank: 21

Last season, Adebayo joined Shaquille O'Neal and Alonzo Mourning as the only Heat players to average 20 points and 10 rebounds in a season. The highlight of Adebayo's campaign came on March 10, when he scored 83 points, the second most in a game in NBA history. The next chapter in his Heat career pairs him with Giannis Antetokounmpo. The two-time MVP and former Buck has experience playing with floor-spacing centers, and Adebayo can provide the same help in Miami. He attempted 400 3-pointers last season, more than his first eight seasons combined. -- Williams

Signature stat: Adebayo's 83-point night was the highest scoring game since Wilt Chamberlain's 100 in March 1962.

Fantasy projection: 20.2 PTS, 10.0 REB, 1.2 STL

27. Deni Avdija
F | Portland Trail Blazers

Age: 25

2025 NBA Rank: 66

Few observers saw Avdija's rapid ascension coming when the Blazers acquired him from the Wizards in a largely overlooked 2024 trade. The punishing wing enjoyed a breakout 2025-26 campaign, posting career highs in scoring, player efficiency rating and win shares while earning his first All-Star selection and leading Portland to the playoffs for the first time in five years. There's more good news: Avdija projects as one of the NBA's best values in 2026-27 given that his bargain $13.1 million salary is less than the midlevel exception. -- Golliver

Signature stat: Avdija finished fourth in NBA in drawing fouls last season, but he was at his best drawing contact in the paint. Avdija drew 267 fouls in the paint, second in the NBA behind Paolo Banchero (275), per Genius IQ.

Fantasy projection: 23.0 PTS, 7.2 REB, 6.3 AST

26. Evan Mobley
F | Cleveland Cavaliers

Age: 25

2025 NBA Rank: 13

The Cavaliers extended Donovan Mitchell, re-signed James Harden and traded for Peyton Watson. But the wild card in how far the Cavaliers go this season could become Mobley. Named Defensive Player of the Year in 2025 (he was also named All-NBA second team), Mobley saw a small dip on the defensive end and regressed offensively. The Cavaliers were plus-5.9 points per 100 possessions with Mobley on the court in the regular season but nearly 10 points worse in the postseason. -- Marks

Signature stat: Since entering the league in 2022, Mobley is one of six players with 400 blocks and 200 steals.

Fantasy projection: 18.9 PTS, 9.8 REB, 1.7 BLK

25. Jalen Williams
G | Oklahoma City Thunder

Age: 25

2025 NBA Rank: 11

Injuries sabotaged Williams' 2025-26 season and ultimately could be the No. 1 reason why we're not talking about the Thunder as back-to-back champs. First, offseason wrist surgery following the title over Indiana caused Williams to miss 19 games to start the regular season, then hamstring strains to both legs sidelined him for most of the postseason. Still only 25, the 6-5 Williams is a three-level scorer who commits on the defensive end. His 3-point accuracy will be an X factor for him this season. He shot 42.7% from deep in 2023-24 but just 29.9% in limited action last year. -- McMenamin

Signature stat: Injuries limited Williams to a career-low 33 games last season, and he played in just five of Thunder's 15 playoff games.

Fantasy projection: 20.6 PTS, 5.3 AST, 1.4 STL

24. Chet Holmgren
C | Oklahoma City Thunder

Age: 24

2025 NBA Rank: 24

Holmgren has the length and timing as a shot blocker to make him the best defender of his generation outside of Wembanyama. Holmgren also has the shooting touch and quickness off the dribble to make him a mismatch for most opposing big men to defend. Holmgren's skill set is so strong, in fact, that the biggest criticism he faces is that he isn't aggressive enough on offense to take advantage of those mismatches. Holmgren remains a pillar for the Thunder, but a shift in offensive mindset could put him on the brink of superstardom. -- Snellings

Signature stat: Last season, Holmgren set career highs in points per game (17.1), rebounds per game (8.9) and field goal percentage (56%).

Fantasy projection: 16.5 PTS, 8.4 REB, 2.1 BLK

23. Cooper Flagg
F | Dallas Mavericks

Age: 19

2025 NBA Rank: 52

Flagg's rookie season began with a whimper, as he struggled to adjust to the NBA while being thrust into the unfamiliar position of point guard. But it ended with a bang at his rightful position of small forward, as a torrid late-season burst -- including back-to-back games with 51 and 45 points in April -- propelled him to his expected Rookie of the Year honor.

The former No. 1 pick doesn't even celebrate his 20th birthday until December, yet he's already one of the best two-way wings in the league, with a strong defensive foundation and a budding offensive skill set. Flagg must improve his jump shot (29.5% on 3s last year), but that might be the only real obstacle standing in the way of an All-Star berth. -- Kram

Signature stat: Flagg is the first teenager in NBA history to record a 50-point game.

Fantasy projection: 22.3 PTS, 7.0 REB, 4.8 AST

22. Jalen Johnson
F | Atlanta Hawks

Age: 24

2025 NBA Rank: 44

The Hawks clearly made the right call by passing the torch from Trae Young to Johnson, who earned his first All-Star selection with an absurdly productive 2025-26 season. The 6-8 forward thrived as a playmaker and finisher in Atlanta's up-tempo attack, and he helped lead the franchise to its most wins since 2015-16. What's more, his plus-3.2 net rating surpassed Young's best mark in any of the previous four seasons. To climb even further up these rankings, the 24-year-old Johnson must prove his game can fully translate to the postseason after an underwhelming series against the Knicks. -- Golliver

Signature stat: Johnson's 13 triple-doubles last season set the Hawks franchise record.

Fantasy projection: 23.0 PTS, 10.6 REB, 7.9 AST

21. Jamal Murray
G | Denver Nuggets

Age: 29

2025 NBA Rank: 46

Murray had one of the bigger jumps in the rankings after being named an All-Star and making All-NBA for the first time in his career. He was the only player to average at least 25 points, seven assists and 40% on 3-pointers in 2025-26. Murray also finished second for Clutch Player of the Year after ranking top two in clutch time points and assists. -- Williams

Signature stat: Last season, Murray set career highs in points per game (25.4), assists per game (7.1) and 3-pointers made (245).

Fantasy projection: 23.1 PTS, 6.6 AST, 4.1 REB

20. Devin Booker
G | Phoenix Suns

Age: 29

2025 NBA Rank: 16

Booker is one of the most malleable stars as the Suns have assembled various teams around him in recent years and yet, he continues to thrive. From teaming with Chris Paul to playing alongside Kevin Durant to now, having Dillon Brooks as a running mate. Pencil him in for 26 points and 6 assists, the ability to play both guard positions and playing through nicks and bruises. His 11 years in the league have been in the Valley, and he's signed through 2029-30 -- a rare one-team star. -- Goodwill

Signature stat: Booker was one of five players with at least 1,000 drives last season and was one of eight players to score 1,000 points when he drove (min. 500 drives), per Genius IQ tracking.

Fantasy projection: 26.5 PTS, 6.7 AST, 4.2 REB

19. Tyrese Haliburton
G | Indiana Pacers

Age: 26

2025 NBA Rank: NR (injury)

Haliburton would have been in the top 15 last year had he not suffered a torn Achilles in Game 7 of the 2025 NBA Finals. On the sidelines for all last season, Haliburton witnessed one of the best offenses plummet in all statistical categories. The Pacers ranked 27th in offensive efficiency, 26th in field goal percentage, 20th in 3-point percentage and 18th in fast-break points. -- Marks

Signature stat: Haliburton has the second-best assist-to-turnover ratio (3.81) in NBA postseason history (min. 300 assists) since individual turnovers were first tracked in 1977-78 (John Paxson, 4.31).

Fantasy projection: 19.2 PTS, 9.9 AST, 1.3 STL

18. LeBron James
F | Philadelphia 76ers

Age: 41

2025 NBA Rank: 8

Seeing James outside the top 10 is jarring. Then again, seeing a guy who turns 42 in a few months still inside the top 25 is probably the better framing to appreciate what the 22-time All-Star continues to accomplish. James already had success as L.A.'s No. 3 option last season and will likely reprise that role behind Tyrese Maxey and Jaylen Brown for the 76ers. The difference is that while James' scoring took a back seat to Doncic and Reaves for the Lakers, his touches might not suffer too much in Philly. Sixers president of basketball operations Mike Gansey has indicated the team will have James play point forward and orchestrate the offense, similar to his role with the Lakers when they won the 2020 title. -- McMenamin

Signature stat: The 41-year-old James finished second in the NBA in fast-break points last season, behind only his new teammate, Tyrese Maxey.

Fantasy projection: 21.0 PTS, 7.0 AST, 6.3 REB

17. Scottie Barnes
F | Toronto Raptors

Age: 25

2025 NBA Rank: 30

Barnes has developed from the 2022 Rookie of the Year to a two-time All-Star entering his sixth season. He has been the do-everything engine for the Raptors on both offense and defense, finishing fifth in the Defensive Player of the Year vote while leading the team in assists and scoring nearly 20 points per game. This season he will join Kawhi Leonard as the nucleus of a Raptors squad that is trying to make the leap from play-in scrappy competitors to playoffs contenders. -- Snellings

Signature stat: Barnes led his team in rebounds, assists, steals and blocks last season. Since 2017-18, LeBron James (2021-22) and Nikola Jokic (2017-18) are the only other players to accomplish the feat.

Fantasy projection: 18.8 PTS, 7.7 REB, 6.0 AST, 1.4 STL

16. Karl-Anthony Towns
C | New York Knicks

Age: 30

2025 NBA Rank: 27

Few players saw their reputations rise as high last season as Towns. Throughout his career, the former No. 1 pick had been dogged by criticisms of his foolish mistakes -- costly turnovers, silly fouls -- and even in the middle of last season, drama swirled about his role in New York's offense under coach Mike Brown.

But that all changed during a magical playoff run, in which Towns made 46% of his 3-point attempts and played the best, most consistent defense of his career en route to a title. He only averaged 16 points during the playoffs, but he was a picture-perfect role player. With Mitchell Robinson gone to Boston in free agency, the Knicks don't have much of a Plan B if Towns' struggles at center return. But he more than proved himself in the postseason. -- Kram

Signature stat: During the Knicks' run to the 2026 title, Towns became the first player in NBA postseason history to record 55/45/90 shooting splits with least 400 minutes played.

Fantasy projection: 21.9 PTS, 11.2 REB, 4.4 AST

15. Kawhi Leonard
F | Toronto Raptors

Age: 35

2025 NBA Rank: 20

Leonard flew the coop to Canada after his seven-season run with the Clippers ended in infamy. While the seven-time All-Star escaped the NBA's salary cap circumvention investigation with only a $700,000 fine, his Raptors reunion will reportedly play out under the cloud of a separate federal investigation. On the court, Leonard posted career highs in points and player efficiency rating last season -- a remarkable feat considering he turned 35 in June. Toronto's young roster should benefit from his championship experience, but Leonard, who hasn't advanced past the first round since 2021, must prove he can still crank it up in the playoffs. -- Golliver

Signature stat: Leonard, who set a career high with 27.9 points per game last season, scored at least 20 in each of his final 57 games for the Clippers. That tied Bob McAdoo for the longest streak in franchise history.

Fantasy projection: 25.1 PTS, 6.2 REB, 1.7 STL

14. Jaylen Brown
F | Philadelphia 76ers

Age: 29

2025 NBA Rank: 19

With Jayson Tatum missing most of the 2025-26 season, Brown posted the third-highest usage rate in the league behind Doncic and Antetokounmpo. He delivered in those minutes, averaging 28.7 points, the fifth most in a season in Celtics history. In addition, Brown became the fourth Celtics player to average 25 points, five rebounds and five assists in a season in franchise history, joining Tatum, Larry Bird and John Havlicek. But the move to the 76ers opens questions about what his usage looks like playing alongside James, Embiid and Maxey. -- Williams

Signature stat: Last season, Brown set career highs in points (28.7), rebounds (6.9), and assists (5.1) per game.

Fantasy projection: 23.9 PTS, 5.9 REB, 4.3 AST

13. Kevin Durant
F | Houston Rockets

Age: 37

2025 NBA Rank: 9

For all the talk of the ageless wonders in the NBA, 38-year-old (on 9/29) Kevin Durant doesn't quite fly under the radar, but his longevity feels somewhat underappreciated. He made the All-NBA team for the 12th time, tied for seventh in the history of the league with the likes of Dirk Nowitzki, Hakeem Olajuwon and Jerry West, among others. Since his right Achilles injury in 2019, he has averaged 27/6/5 on 53/41/88 splits. He helped keep the Rockets afloat in his first season, but they flamed out in the first round against the Lakers. Durant is a leader by example, and this seemed to conflict with the youth on the roster at times. Do the Rockets have enough leadership, and will he have enough gas in a top-heavy West? -- Goodwill

Signature stat: Durant enters 2026-27 on a four-season streak of at least 25 points per game, 50% shooting from the field and 40% shooting from 3. No other player has more than three such seasons for their career.

Fantasy projection: 25.0 PTS, 5.6 REB, 4.4 AST

12. Stephen Curry
G | Golden State Warriors

Age: 38

2025 NBA Rank: 7

Durability concerns have Curry falling out of the top 10. After missing most of the 2025 second round with a hamstring injury, Curry played the third-fewest games of his career in 2025-26. (He missed 29 games after Jan. 24 with a right knee injury.) Managing Curry's minutes will be key even with Jimmy Butler III and Moses Moody out an extended period. Last season, he averaged his fewest minutes of the past six seasons. The 38-year-old is eligible to sign up to a two-year, $137 million extension. -- Marks

Signature stat: Curry has 26,528 career points with Warriors, third most with a single franchise in NBA history behind Kobe Bryant (33,643 with Lakers) and Dirk Nowitzki (31,560 with Mavericks).

Fantasy projection: 25.8 PTS, 5.3 AST, 4.2 REB, 4.6 3PM

11. Tyrese Maxey
G | Philadelphia 76ers

Age: 25

2025 NBA Rank: 28

Maxey's scoring average has increased in each of his six seasons in the league, topping out at 28.3 points per game last season (No. 5 in the league) to earn him an All-NBA third team selection. It cannot be overstated how much Maxey's presence factored into LeBron James' decision to sign with the 76ers, and it will be on the 25-year-old combo guard to make James and Jaylen Brown feel welcome, while still maximizing the holdover talents of Embiid and VJ Edgecombe. There's nothing about Maxey's game or personality that would suggest that he won't be able to continue to thrive with the spotlight even brighter this season. -- McMenamin

Signature stat: Maxey has increased his points per game and 3-point percentage in each season of his NBA career.

Fantasy projection: 24.8 PTS, 5.8 AST, 1.6 STL

stories.headline: Sources: Panthers RB Jonathon Brooks set for surgery, IR move
stories.summary: Panthers running back Jonathon Brooks is expected to undergo surgery to repair a core muscle injury and is set to miss at least six weeks, sources told NFL Network.
stories.body:
Carolina Panthers running back Jonathon Brooks is expected to undergo core muscle surgery Wednesday and land on injured reserve, sources told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.

He will be sidelined for at least six weeks, sources said.

Brooks left Sunday's win over the Atlanta Falcons in the fourth quarter with what was described as a groin injury. The third-year running back walked to the tunnel with a towel over his head with three members of the Panthers' staff. He was later seen favoring the injury as he slowly limped, on his own power, to the locker room following the game.

Brooks, a second-round pick in 2024, returned this season from back-to-back ACL surgeries. He missed the bulk of his rookie season while recovering from the first surgery on his right knee, an injury that occurred during his final year at Texas. After playing in just three games as a rookie, he retore his right ACL in December 2024 and was forced to undergo another procedure, which sidelined him for the entire 2025 season.

He took part in training camp and the preseason this summer for the first time in his NFL career. He sustained a groin injury leading up to Week 1 but was able to play against the Chicago Bears in the season opener.

In two games this season, Brooks produced 30 rushing yards on nine carries and 43 receiving yards on two catches.

With Brooks sidelined for at least six weeks, the best-case scenario might mean he misses only five games, as the Panthers have an early bye in Week 5.

The Panthers have leaned heavily on veteran Chuba Hubbard as the starting running back this season. Hubbard has rushed for 102 yards and a touchdown and caught five passes for 49 yards and two touchdowns. He will continue to carry the load in the backfield with veteran AJ Dillon serving as a change-of-pace option.

Carolina will need to find a third running back for depth. Anthony Tyus III has been on the practice squad in each of the past two seasons, and he was featured heavily throughout the preseason. Ahmani Marshall, a second-year running back, is also on the practice squad.

stories.headline: Zack Wheeler fans 7 straight to open Phillies win over Brewers
stories.summary: Zack Wheeler struck out 11, including seven in a row to start the game, and Bryson Stott hit a tiebreaking single with two outs in the eighth inning as the Phillies inched closer to clinching a playoff spot with a 6-4 victory over the Brewers.
stories.body:
Zack Wheeler struck out 11, including seven in a row to start the game, and Bryson Stott hit a tiebreaking single with two outs in the eighth inning as the Philadelphia Phillies inched closer to clinching a playoff spot with a 6-4 victory over the Milwaukee Brewers on Tuesday night.

Wheeler reached 2,000 career strikeouts when he fanned Brice Turang to end the first, becoming the 96th pitcher in MLB history to reach the milestone.

"Just being where I am now, it's pretty special," Wheeler said of the career milestone, according to MLB.com. "It's a huge thank you to all the catchers that I've had along the way that helped me get here, the coaches and the guys that played behind me. It means a lot to me, and I really appreciate everybody's effort around it."

Unhittable at the outset, Wheeler had sights on Pablo López's MLB record of nine strikeouts in a row to open a contest before Cooper Pratt grounded out to third base for the second out of the third inning.

"I didn't know what to expect coming out," Wheeler said. "Just one of those days for me."

Wheeler is the only Phillies pitcher since 1900 with seven straight strikeouts to start a game, according to the Elias Sports Bureau. Watching Wheeler from the dugout was teammate Aaron Nola, who has a share of the MLB record with 10 consecutive strikeouts of the New York Mets in 2021.

Brandon Marsh homered, doubled and drove in three runs for Philadelphia, which is tied with the Chicago Cubs and San Diego Padres at 87-70 for the three National League wild cards -- four games ahead of the Arizona Diamondbacks with five to play. The Phillies hold a tiebreaker over the Padres but not the Cubs.

William Contreras had three RBIs for NL Central champion Milwaukee. The Brewers, by virtue of Cincinnati's 4-0 win over Atlanta, clinched a bye in the wild-card round and earned home-field advantage for the division series. The Brewers dropped to 13-6 this month and were not able to extend their franchise record of 98 wins, set in Sunday's 3-0 victory at Baltimore.

After the Brewers scored twice in the sixth inning off Wheeler to tie the game at 3, Stott singled to center off Colton Gordon (0-1). Garrett Mitchell's throw went to third base to try to get Alec Bohm running from first, but the ball ricocheted off Bohm's foot and both he and Luis Arraez scored to make it 5-3.

Jhoan Duran earned his 33rd save after Jose Alvarado (5-3) got the final out of the eighth.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

stories.headline: The performance bonuses for Van, Tsarukyan? Spots in P4P top 10
stories.summary: Former UFC champion puts elite status of women's flyweight division on display in ESPN's P4P top 10.
stories.body:
UFC 331 delivered some remarkable performances, a couple of which landed fighters in the ESPN pound-for-pound rankings.

One of them is not heavyweight Sean Sharaf, despite him pulling off the biggest upset in UFC history with his 12-second knockout of mega-prospect Gable Steveson. Women's flyweight Casey O'Neill produced a leading candidate for submission of the year, escaping a dangerous position to quickly armbar Eduarda Moura, but that didn't earn O'Neill a top-10 spot, either.

Both of those fighters were eye openers, but the rankings were reserved for the two winners of Saturday's headline fights.

In the main event, Joshua Van successfully defended his men's flyweight title against former champion Alexandre Pantoja, using crisp boxing and efficient grappling to secure a unanimous decision. Van moves into the men's rankings at No. 8, and Pantoja, who previously occupied that position, drops out.

Also earning a top-10 spot is co-main event winner Arman Tsarukyan, who knocked out flashy striker Mauricio Ruffy to all but secure a lightweight title shot. Tsarukyan moves in at No. 10, with former light heavyweight champion Alex Pereira falling from the rankings.

For the ESPN divisional MMA rankings, click here.

Note: Results are current; rankings are as of Sept. 23. To be eligible for the rankings, a fighter must have competed over the past 12 months or must have an upcoming fight booked. Fighters who have been dropped for inactivity can be reinstated only after they compete.

Men's pound-for-pound rankings

1. Islam Makhachev

UFC welterweight champion

Record: 29-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Ian Machado Garry, Aug. 15

Next: TBA

Makhachev vacated the UFC lightweight championship to go for a second title at welterweight. By winning that belt last November with a thrashing of Jack Della Maddalena, Makhachev staked his place among MMA's greatest -- not just in today's sport but of all time. His win over Machado Garry at UFC 330 was his 17th straight, breaking the UFC record for consecutive wins. Makhachev is piling up unprecedented achievements.

2. Petr Yan

UFC bantamweight champion

Record: 20-5

Last: W (UD) vs. Merab Dvalishvili, Dec. 6, 2025

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Dvalishvili

What a return to the top it's been for Yan. He began his career with 15 consecutive wins before going on a 1-4 run from 2021 to 2023. That almost doesn't feel real now, after watching him reclaim his throne against Dvalishvili, who once handed him the worst loss of his career. Yan took a major detour, but this was the destination we felt he was capable of before the skid. He once again looks like one of the best fighters on the planet. He can prove it by beating Dvalishvili again.

3. Merab Dvalishvili

UFC bantamweight

Record: 21-5

Last: L (UD) vs. Petr Yan, Dec. 6, 2025

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Yan

Dvalishvili was on one of the most impressive runs through the UFC's bantamweight division ever. Not only did he defeat Sean O'Malley for the second time in nine months at UFC 316, but he showcased a new part of his game, finishing O'Malley with a guillotine. Starting in August 2022, Dvalishvili beat José Aldo, Yan, Henry Cejudo, O'Malley (twice), Umar Nurmagomedov and Cory Sandhagen. But at UFC 323, in an attempt to become the first champion in UFC history to successfully defend a title four times in a calendar year, Dvalishvili lost a rematch with Yan. They will fight for a third time at UFC 333.

T-4. Tom Aspinall

UFC heavyweight

Record: 15-3, 1 NC

Last: NC1 vs. Ciryl Gane, Oct. 25, 2025

Next: TBA

You can make a case that Aspinall is the most dynamic, skillful, talented heavyweight the sport has seen. He is dominating opponents in a way that is unmatched. No one can last a round with him. He had hoped to prove his supremacy against Jon Jones, but Jones opted to retire, elevating Aspinall from interim champion. His first defense of the undisputed belt ended anticlimactically, as an eye poke resulted in his UFC 321 fight with Gane being declared a no-contest. Still recovering from the eye injury, Aspinall vacated his title on Sept. 14.

T-4. Justin Gaethje

UFC lightweight champion

Previous ranking: 6

Record: 28-5

Last: W (TKO4) vs. Ilia Topuria, June 14

Next: TBA

Gaethje has spent his 15-year career thrilling MMA fans, but before the title bout on the White House lawn, all he had to show for it -- aside from 15 bonus checks in 15 UFC appearances -- were two missed opportunities to be an undisputed champion. His fourth-round TKO of Topuria got Gaethje over the hump. It was a resilient performance in a back-and-forth battle that is a prime candidate for fight of the year. More important for Gaethje: At age 37, he is finally sitting at the top of the mountain.

6. Ilia Topuria

UFC lightweight

Previous ranking: 5

Record: 17-1

Last: L (TKO4) vs. Justin Gaethje, June 14

Next: TBA

Topuria was an undefeated two-division champion when he ran into Gaethje at UFC Freedom 250 and was brutalized in a stoppage loss. How will that affect the immediate future of Topuria? His knockout wins over two of the greatest featherweights, Alexander Volkanovski and Max Holloway, gave him an intimidating aura. Can the former champion get that back?

7. Alexander Volkanovski

UFC featherweight champion

Record: 28-4

Last: W (UD) vs. Diego Lopes, Jan. 31

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Movsar Evloev

It felt as if the sport had started to write Volkanovski's eulogy following his knockout loss to Ilia Topuria in February 2024. Volkanovski noticed and made a point of proving to everyone he still has plenty left by recapturing the featherweight belt at UFC 314, the first of two consecutive wins over Lopes. His age (37) will likely continue to be a prefight topic, which is fine because Volkanovski enjoys proving people wrong. Can he hand Evloev his first loss at UFC 333?

8. Joshua Van

UFC flyweight champion

Previous ranking: Unranked

Record: 18-2

Last: W (UD) vs. Alexandre Pantoja, Sept. 19

Next: TBA

Van has been champion since December, but until UFC 331, there were doubters. Van had been handed the belt by default, when his challenge for the title was waved off after 26 seconds because Pantoja dislocated his left elbow. Van went on to defend the title against Tatsuro Taira in May, then faced Pantoja in a rematch this past weekend. Van produced a clear victory -- his eighth win in a row -- to leave no doubt who rules at 125 pounds.

9. Ciryl Gane

UFC heavyweight champion

Record: 14-2, 1 NC

Last: W (TKO2) vs. Alex Pereira, June 14

Next: Nov. 14 vs. Josh Hokit

Gane is unique in that he is the first -- and could very well go down as the only -- heavyweight to face the division's four biggest names in Francis Ngannou, Jon Jones, Tom Aspinall and Pereira. None of those four have fought each other, yet all four have have fought the Frenchman. Gane was 0-2 with a no-contest against that group before he knocked out Pereira in the second round of their interim title fight. Gane was elevated to undisputed champ after Aspinall, still injured, vacated his title, and the new champ will defend against Hokit at UFC 334.

10. Arman Tsarukyan

UFC lightweight

Previous ranking: Unranked

Record: 24-3

Last: W (KO1) vs. Mauricio Ruffy, Sept. 19

Next: TBA

Tsarukyan is right back in the place he was in January 2025 -- on the cusp of a title fight. He withdrew from that challenge of Islam Makhachev one day before UFC 311 because of a back injury, and later in the year he was passed over twice when the UFC was booking lightweight title bouts. But by knocking out Mauricio Ruffy with an elbow in the first round at UFC 331, Tsarukyan put himself back at the front of the line.

Other fighter receiving votes: Alex Pereira.

How our panel voted
Brett Okamoto: 1. Islam Makhachev; 2. Petr Yan; 3. Merab Dvalishvili; 4. Ilia Topuria; 5. Alexander Volkanovski; 6. Joshua Van; 7. Arman Tsarukyan; 8. Ciryl Gane; 9. Alex Pereira; 10. Justin Gaethje.

Carlos Contreras Legaspi: 1. Makhachev; 2. Volkanovski; 3. Gaethje; 4. Topuria; 5. Pereira; 6. Dvalishvili; 7. Van; 8. Gane; 9. Yan; 10. Tsarukyan.

Andrew Davis: 1. Makhachev; 2. Tom Aspinall; 3. Yan; 4. Dvalishvili; 5. Gaethje; 6. Topuria; 7. Volkanovski; 8. Van; 9. Gane; 10. Tsarukyan.

Dre Waters: 1. Makhachev; 2. Aspinall; 3. Yan; 4. Dvalishvili; 5. Gaethje; 6. Volkanovski; 7. Topuria; 8. Van; 9. Gane; 10. Pereira.

Jeff Wagenheim: 1. Makhachev; 2. Aspinall; 3. Yan; 4. Van; 5. Gaethje; 6. Dvalishvili; 7. Tsarukyan; 8. Topuria; 9. Gane; 10. Volkanovski.

Women's pound-for-pound rankings

1. Valentina Shevchenko

UFC flyweight

Record: 26-4-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Zhang Weili, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: TBA

Shevchenko's dominance came under question in 2022 and 2023, when she went 1-1-1 in a trilogy with Alexa Grasso. Boy, does that feel like a long time ago now. Shevchenko more than reasserted herself as the best flyweight in the world, and then she established herself as the No. 1 woman in the world, period. It wasn't surprising that she beat Zhang, but it was surprising how easy she made it look. Shevchenko is out injured, however, so she has vacated her UFC title, which will be up for grabs when Natalia Silva meets Wang Cong on Oct. 3.

2. Zhang Weili

UFC flyweight / strawweight

Record: 26-4

Last: L (UD) vs. Valentina Shevchenko, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: TBA

It's hard to move up in weight, especially at the highest level. That sounds like it should be obvious, but Zhang had been dominant at 115 pounds for so long, some of us might have taken for granted how big of a challenge moving to 125 would be. UFC 322 was a bad night for Zhang, but she doesn't have many. And if she decides to stay at flyweight, it certainly seems reasonable to believe she'll fare better in the future.

3. Cris Cyborg

PFL featherweight champion

Record: 30-2, 1 NC

Last: W (UD) vs. Ketlen Vieira, Aug. 22

Next: TBA

It had been a while since Cyborg had fought an elite opponent in MMA until she met Larissa Pacheco in 2024. That was a legitimate matchup -- and many within the industry were predicting Cyborg's downfall. Instead, she took out the PFL's two-weight champion, upending all of Pacheco's momentum. One of the original pioneers of women's MMA is once again a champion after getting her second career submission at PFL Lyon in December. The PFL promoted her fight with Vieira as a retirement bout, but after her win Cyborg did not sound like someone who is done fighting.

4. Mackenzie Dern

UFC strawweight champion

Record: 17-5

Last: W (UD) vs. Gillian Robertson, Aug. 15

Next: TBA

Dern's rise to the 115-pound throne was truly a changing of the guard. She is the division's first first-time champion since 2019, because the previous three champs -- Zhang Weili, Carla Esparza and Rose Namajunas -- all were in their second reigns. Dern, nearly a decade into her MMA career after multiple jiu-jitsu world championships, has won four fights in a row, including a dominant performance against a fellow grappling-heavy fighter, Robertson, in her first title defense.

5. Natalia Silva

UFC flyweight

Record: 20-5-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Rose Namajunas, Jan. 24

Next: Oct. 3 vs. Wang Cong

Silva is looking every bit the part of a future UFC champion following a dominant display against Alexa Grasso at UFC 315 and a victory over Namajunas at UFC 324. Silva's stick-and-move style has frustrated even the highest level of opponent, and she's got youth on her side as she won't turn 30 until 2027. With an injured Valentina Shevchenko having vacated the title, Silva will fight Wang for the belt at UFC 332.

6. Alexa Grasso

UFC flyweight

Previous ranking: 10

Record: 18-5-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Manon Fiorot, Sept. 12

Next: TBA

Grasso went nearly three years without winning a fight, but her 2023 win right before the skid was a huge one, a submission of Valentina Shevchenko for the UFC title. What followed were two more fights with Shevchenko -- a draw, then a loss -- and then a loss to Natalia Silva. But she reasserted herself with a finish of Maycee Barber in March, then got the best of Fiorot, a fellow title contender, at Noche UFC to put herself in position for another title shot.

7. Dakota Ditcheva

PFL flyweight

Record: 16-0

Last: W (UD) vs. Denise Kielholtz, July 31

Next: TBA

Not only did Ditcheva win the PFL's flyweight season in 2024, but she did so in spectacular fashion -- a TKO finish over Taila Santos, who once challenged for a UFC title. Ditcheva fought only once in 2025, dominating Sumiko Inaba in the co-main event of the first PFL Champions Series card in Cape Town, South Africa. She then spent over a year on the sideline, healing injuries to both hands, before returning at PFL New York with a dominant win over Kielholtz.

8. Manon Fiorot

UFC flyweight

Previous ranking: 6

Record: 13-3

Last: L (UD) vs. Alexa Grasso, Sept. 12

Next: TBA

Fiorot had handled everyone the UFC put in front of her -- except the champion, Valentina Shevchenko, who defeated the Frenchwoman at UFC 315 in May 2025. But then, with another title shot within her grasp, Fiorot ran into Grasso, a former champion, at Noche UFC and lost a competitive fight.

9. Erin Blanchfield

UFC flyweight

Previous ranking: 8

Record: 14-2

Last: W (Sub2) vs. Tracy Cortez, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: Oct. 17 vs. Jasmine Jasudavicius

Her rise toward the top of the division was derailed by a March 2024 loss to Manon Fiorot, but Blanchfield bounced back with two straight wins, including one over two-time former strawweight champion Rose Namajunas in November 2024. If she wins her October bout with Jasudavicius, a fellow top-10 flyweight contender, Blanchfield would inch ever closer to a title shot.

10. Tatiana Suarez

UFC strawweight

Previous ranking: 9

Record: 12-1

Last: W (Sub2) vs. Loopy Godínez, April 11

Next: TBA

If Suarez is still feeling the effects of last year's humbling defeat to Zhang Weili in a title challenge, she certainly didn't show it at UFC 327, overcoming early adversity to thrash Godinez, a fellow top-10 strawweight. Suarez is going to be a tough out for anyone at 115 pounds.

How our panel voted
Brett Okamoto: 1. Valentina Shevchenko; 2. Zhang Weili; 3. Mackenzie Dern; 4. Cris Cyborg; 5. Alexa Grasso; 6. Manon Fiorot; 7. Dakota Ditcheva; 8. Natalia Silva; 9. Erin Blanchfield; 10. Tatiana Suarez.

Carlos Contreras Legaspi: 1. Shevchenko; 2. Cyborg; 3. Zhang; 4. Dern; 5. Silva; 6. Grasso; 7. Ditcheva; 8. Suarez; 9. Fiorot; 10. Blanchfield.

Andrew Davis: 1. Shevchenko; 2. Zhang; 3. Cyborg; 4. Dern; 5. Silva; 6. Grasso; 7. Blanchfield; 8. Ditcheva; 9. Suarez; 10. Fiorot.

Dre Waters: 1. Shevchenko; 2. Zhang; 3. Cyborg; 4. Silva; 5. Dern; 6. Grasso; 7. Ditcheva; 8. Blanchfield; 9. Fiorot; 10. Suarez.

Jeff Wagenheim: 1. Shevchenko; 2. Zhang; 3. Cyborg; 4. Silva; 5. Grasso; 6. Dern; 7. Fiorot; 8. Blanchfield; 9. Suarez; 10. Ditcheva.

stories.headline: Haas' Esteban Ocon future in F1 unclear: 'Free agent' for 2027 season
stories.summary: Esteban Ocon has hinted he might leave Haas at the end of the season, saying "at the moment" he's a free agent for 2027.
stories.body:
Esteban Ocon has hinted he might leave Haas at the end of the season, saying "at the moment" he's a free agent for 2027.

Ocon joined Haas in 2025 but struggled to perform against teammate Oliver Bearman and only just managed to hold his seat coming into this year. Sources told ESPN that Haas were close to bringing in Yuki Tsunoda in his place for this season.

Despite that second chance, Ocon's performances have not improved this year -- he has three points to Bearman's 18 -- and it has seemed increasingly likely he will not be retained for a third season.

Brazilian Formula 2 driver Rafael Camara, 21, is believed to be the frontrunner to partner Bearman next season, while the team also recently handed a test to McLaren junior driver Leonardo Foronoli.

Speaking ahead of this week's Azerbaijan Grand Prix, Ocon said talks about his future are wide open.

"At the moment I'm definitely a free agent for next year," Ocon is quoted as saying by Autosport and other outlets from his Baku media session. "There are things in discussion that are out of my control. There are certain topics that are out of my control. So I will keep pushing until the end of the year and see how it goes."

Asked if staying at Haas is still an option, Ocon said simply: "Let's see."

Haas is not expected to make a 2027 driver announcement this week.

Ocon might turn out to be the first major mover in this season's driver market, which has been remarkably static.

Most teams are continuing with their existing line-ups -- on Wednesday Red Bull confirmed an extension for the returning Isack Hadjar, keeping him with Max Verstappen for another year, while Fernando Alonso is widely expected to remain with Aston Martin for another season, although he is yet to make a decision.

Cadillac might represent the only F1 race seat available to Ocon, with Valtteri Bottas looking unlikely to stay beyond 2026 -- however, sources have told ESPN that F1's newest team is still keen to give American driver Colton Herta an opportunity alongside Sergio Pérez.

Ocon, 30, is in his 10th season of racing in Formula 1, having debuted with Manor in 2016.

As a youngster the French driver was considered one of the sport's future superstars, beating a young Verstappen to the 2014 Formula 3 European Championship.

He was a Mercedes junior driver in the early days of his career but never quite lived up to the lofty billing.

His sole F1 win came for Alpine at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix.

stories.headline: Bounceback picks: The fantasy hockey stars looking to turn back the clock
stories.summary: Here are the fantasy hockey players poised to return to past success, and others you should be wary of.
stories.body:
Even Connor McDavid has a down year in him.

In 2024-25, the best player alive slipped from 3.21 fantasy points per game (FPPG) the year prior to 2.60, the kind of "collapse" that would be a career year for almost anyone else. Then he did what the genuinely elite tend to do after a dip: climbed right back to 3.21. If it can happen to McDavid, it can happen to whichever name on your roster you spent last spring apologizing for.

That's the whole bounceback game; separating the skaters who are actually declining from the ones who just caught a bad hand of variance, injuries or linemate roulette, and are now sitting a round or two cheaper than they should be because of it.

Going back to 2009-10, 59 forwards clearing a career mark of 1.7 FPPG have suffered a real down season -- a drop of 0.35 FPPG or more -- and later climbed back above their career average, a feat they pulled off 78 times between them. Some made a career of it: Evgeni Malkin bounced back four separate times, Matt Duchene an almost comical five. The blue line tells the same story, just rarer -- 20 defenders have done it off that same 1.7 bar, with Kris Letang, Roman Josi, Ryan Pulock and Shayne Gostisbehere each rebounding twice. Fewer names, which is exactly why a bouncing-back defender is worth chasing: the position is thin enough that buying one back at a discount can swing your whole season.

And you don't need the archives for proof. Last season alone, Jason Robertson, Mikko Rantanen, Mika Zibanejad and Zach Hyman shook off ugly 2024-25 campaigns up front, while Charlie McAvoy, Adam Fox, Noah Dobson and Brock Faber did the exact same on the back end. Every one of them rewarded whoever drafted them at a discount.

Not every name below carries that 1.7 pedigree, a few are cheaper bets where a bad year has buried a genuinely useful player, but the shape is identical. Down season, recovery profile, discount at the table. Because this is about fantasy value, period, not star power.

So don't overthink the down year. Below are the forwards and defense primed for a possible return to value with a verdict on whether I think the dip is an opportunity or an obituary.

More: Sign up for free | Rankings | Projections | League types

Bounce-back forwards

Auston Matthews, C, Toronto Maple Leafs (29.0 years old, FPPG career/2024-25/last season 2.89/2.98/2.56): The offense stalled without Mitch Marner. Starved of setups, Matthews opened with just 15 goals in the first three months, ranking a very un-Matthews-like 38th in the league. He later endured a stretch of 12 games with no goals before finally scoring in the same game that Radko Gudas ended his season early. The end result was a season capped at 60 games (27 goals, 53 points). But the finish still plays -- he was sixth in the league in shots per minute -- and if Gavin McKenna even partly fills the Marner void, the setups return and the knee is the only thing that has to heal.

Verdict: A clean yes. Matthews is a Rocket Richard-threat at a discount because of a lost year. Just confirm the knee checks out at camp. If it does, don't let him slip out of the first round.

Mitch Marner, RW, Vegas Golden Knights (29.3 years old, FPPG career/2024-25/last season 2.20/2.33/1.96): Year 1 in Vegas was a soft landing, not a letdown, as he drove a line all season and then led the entire NHL in playoff scoring once it counted. He settles in beside William Karlsson on the second line and onto a dangerous power play that has minutes to spare now that Pavel Dorofeyev is gone. Losing Dorofeyev's finishing touch is a concern, not a dealbreaker. Marner will find a new muse.

Verdict: The question is whether he'll be good or trend back toward great. Luckily, the floor on Marner is still a top-50 forward, so it's not as if there is much downside to banking on a bigger season.

J.T. Miller, C/LW, New York Rangers (33.5 years old, FPPG career/2024-25/last season 1.92/2.23/1.82): His first full season back in New York was swallowed by injuries and a team-wide scoring drought, but he found his game in the second half and posted fantasy relevant totals in March and April. With Vincent Trocheck traded to Utah, Miller is finally locked into the full-time center role he prefers behind Mika Zibanejad instead of shuffling to the wing.

Verdict: Role clarity plus health makes him a strong middle-rounds target. He's 33, so don't chase the peak, but 70-plus points is very much on the table.

Brayden Point, C/RW, Tampa Bay Lightning (30.5 years old, FPPG career/2024-25/last season 2.08/2.38/1.57): The bet here is murkier than it looks. Point missed 19 games and his counting stats cratered -- 18 goals, a career-low 14.0 shooting percentage -- but he waved off injuries as the cause at season's end, saying instead that his game has to evolve as he ages. That's honest, and a little worrying: a healthy-but-declining 30-year-old is a different draft proposition than a hurt one bouncing back. Counterpoint, he's still centering Nikita Kucherov and Jake Guentzel on a top power play, so the setups and volume are there if the finish returns.

Verdict: A calculated gamble, not a slam-dunk yes. The talent and linemates argue for a rebound, as his own words argue caution. Fine as a mid-round dart if he slips - but don't pay for the 40-goal ceiling on faith.

Jesper Bratt, RW, New Jersey Devils (28.1 years old, FPPG career/2024-25/last season 1.70/2.18/1.73): He didn't decline so much as shed 14 points of power-play production and some of Jack Hughes' availability, though the even-strength chemistry with Hughes never went anywhere. With Hughes healthy, the scoring should climb. The wrinkle is the power play: New Jersey added top-six wing depth this offseason without subtracting any, so Bratt's man-advantage looks aren't the lock they were. He has to earn the PP1 time that drove his best years, not inherit it.

Verdict: A rebound bet with a catch. Healthy Hughes lifts his even-strength floor, but the crowded forward group puts his power-play ceiling in play, and the PP is where his upside lives.

Nazem Kadri, C/LW, Colorado Avalanche (35.9 years old, FPPG career/2024-25/last season 1.70/1.95/1.52): The down year was a slog on a bad Calgary team plus a deadline move, and the Colorado reunion hands him far better company to keep. The catch is the depth chart: he projects behind Nathan MacKinnon and Brock Nelson at center, so his ceiling hinges on top-six looks and power-play time.

Verdict: The environment upgrade is real, but temper it. Take him as a mid-round multi-category center, not a star. If coach Jared Bednar commits him to a scoring role, the 20-goal, 60-point version is back.

Tomas Hertl, C, Vegas Golden Knights (32.8 years old, FPPG career/2024-25/last season 1.80/2.19/1.81): He slid back to about his career rate, and the real drag is depth-chart gravity. In Vegas's loaded top nine, he's the third-line center behind Jack Eichel and William Karlsson. What rescues his value is the power play, where he's locked onto the top unit.

Verdict: A quietly reliable rebound driven almost entirely by PP1. He won't win your league, but he'll out-earn his cost; grab him once the top center tiers clear.

Dylan Strome, C, Washington Capitals (29.5 years old, FPPG career/2024-25/last season 1.64/2.10/1.62): He's still Washington's top-line pivot, but everything cooled at once last year. Those are classic bounce-back signals, and the Capitals added Jordan Kyrou and Alex Tuch to deepen the scoring around him, and they might even end up flanking him full-time.

Verdict: A textbook draft-low: same premium role, colder-than-real results. Target him in the middle rounds and expect a return to the 70-point neighborhood.

Jordan Kyrou, RW, Washington Capitals (28.3 years old, FPPG career/2024-25/last season 1.69/1.97/1.44): A trade to Washington is a fresh start after his shooting percentage bottomed out, but the shot volume never did. He ranked 31st in the league in shots per 60 last season, right in the mix with names like Kirill Kaprizov and Kyle Connor, so the finishing slump reads as variance, not decline. He arrives a three-time 30-goal scorer built for sheltered, offensive-zone minutes, whether he lines up with Pierre-Luc Dubois or slots up alongside Strome.

Verdict: Believe the goal rebound with one caveat -- the top power-play spot is a rotation, so his special-teams points aren't locked. A mid-round price for a run back at 30 goals is worth it.

Valeri Nichushkin, RW, Columbus Blue Jackets (31.5 years old, FPPG career/2024-25/last season 1.42/2.02/1.44): He lands in Columbus off a down year, and the draw is real: he ranked 28th in the NHL in goals per game over the four seasons prior to falling off. The knocks are real, too, though: he only played 212 of the 328 games in those four years, and Columbus is jammed with middle-six forwards fighting for the same minutes.

Verdict: A boom-or-bust multi-category flier. If he wins a top-six job and stays on the ice, the draft spot is a steal. Take him late and be ready to move on if the role wavers.

John Tavares, C, Toronto Maple Leafs (36.0 years old, FPPG career/2024-25/last season 2.11/2.31/1.84): The production didn't just dip, it fell off his own career pace, from 2.31 the year before to 1.84, his leanest full season in years. But the role that made him useful is intact: he anchors a second line with William Nylander, remains a power-play fixture and still gets his net-front goals. At 36 the age is real, but a half-point below his career rate is steeper than his usage says it should be.

Verdict: A modest bounce-back on role alone - the Nylander line and power-play time argue the 1.84 was low, not the new normal.

Alex Ovechkin, LW/RW, Washington Capitals (41.0 years old, FPPG career/2024-25/last season 2.61/2.60/1.85): Even at 41 he led Washington in goals and didn't miss a game. The collapse was specifically on the power play, where his shooting percentage fell off a cliff (a career-low five power-play goals) while the unit kept generating chances at his usual rate. He still owns a top power-play role, and the Jordan Kyrou and Alex Tuch additions should feed the setups.

Verdict: The volume and PP1 real estate make a goal rebound likely; believe in the shot totals and expect the man-advantage finishing to normalize - just don't expect that 2024-25 magic to return.

Made it this far? Create your own league with your own rules and play against your friends today.

Bounce-back defense

MacKenzie Weegar, D, Utah Mammoth (32.7 years old, FPPG career/2024-25/last season 1.93/2.51/1.96): His rate dipped thanks to the fantasy void of Calgary and the deeper Utah blue line after he was traded, but he eventually settled in next to Mikhail Sergachev on the top pair and looked the part by the postseason. He's a true multi-category starter, as he finished the past three seasons ranked second or third in the league in fantasy points from hits and blocked shots combined.

Verdict: A solid rebound with one ceiling-cap: Sergachev runs the top power play, so Weegar's points lean even-strength. He can still be a No. 2 defender for fantasy thanks to his elite peripherals.

Shea Theodore, D, Vegas Golden Knights (31.1 years old, FPPG career/2024-25/last season 1.73/1.91/1.54): His power-play value slipped when Vegas leaned on a five-forward attack most nights. And when they did run a defenseman up top, the job stopped being his alone. After Rasmus Andersson arrived at the deadline, the two split the blue line's power-play minutes almost evenly across the games they both dressed. Theodore led on some nights, Andersson on others, and on a couple even Noah Hanifin topped them both. The PP1 role went from Theodore's to a committee.

Verdict: Don't draft Theodore as a lock for power-play quarterback minutes. He'll get them if Vegas backs off the five-forward look, but he has to hold off a legitimate top-pair talent in Andersson, and last year the split was closer to even than settled.

Colton Parayko, D, St. Louis Blues (33.3 years old, FPPG career/2024-25/last season 1.83/2.34/1.66): His ceiling season was inflated by a shooting percentage twice his career norm, and last year's slide came with back and knee trouble plus a more purely defensive assignment. The peripherals are dependable, like top-pair minutes, penalty-kill time and 160-plus blocks.

Verdict: Expect a multi-category floor, not a goal repeat, because the 16-goal spike isn't the baseline. A late-round blocks-and-shots defender who's far more valuable in banger and category leagues than points-only.

Victor Hedman, D, Tampa Bay Lightning (35.7 years old, FPPG career/2024-25/last season 2.06/2.31/1.51): His down year came with the season ending early when he stepped away from the team for personal reasons, not from any erosion of his game. The complication for 2026-27 is new arrival John Carlson, who projects onto the top unit and could split the power-play quarterback minutes.

Verdict: Let someone else pay for the name. The talent still says rebound if he's back and right, but that's the problem. It's one "if" stacked on two more: he turns 36 this season and Carlson's arrival threatens power-play minutes. Any one of those is manageable; all three at a Hedman price is a pick you don't need to make.

stories.headline: Banned Sydney Swans players apologise to AFL club
stories.summary: The five suspended Sydney Swans players have returned to club headquarters for the first time since sexual assault allegations emerged from a post-match party.
stories.body:
Sydney's five suspended players have offered an apology to teammates and colleagues after ending their weeks-long exile from the AFL club.

Swans vice-captain Isaac Heeney, Chad Warner, Nick Blakey, James Jordon and Riley Bice on Wednesday appeared at Swans HQ for the first time since being banned for breaching club standards in August.

Each individually spoke and apologised to staff and the club's AFL and AFLW playing lists.

Heeney was the only player after the club meeting to address media, doing so with a brief statement.

"It was really nice to address the whole club," he said on Wednesday evening.

"I was thankful they could give us their time and understanding, so yeah, it was really good."

Warner and Bice first arrived together at the club's base at Moore Park, followed by vice-captain Heeney, Blakey and Jordon in the same car.

Only Heeney and Warner spoke to media upon arriving.

Warner, flanked by a silent Bice, said he was "just here for my exit interview".

Asked if he was going to say sorry or anything at all, Warner said: "I don't know."

Heeney did not answer when he was asked if he had a message to fans.

The five have not spoken in public since a club statement was issued following their round 23 match against Essendon in August.

Their club-imposed suspensions are separate from a police investigation into sexual assault allegations.

No charges have been laid, and AAP is not suggesting any wrongdoing on the part of the five suspended players.

All five are contracted for next year, with Blakey signed to the club until 2031.

Warner and Jordon come off contract at the end of 2027, while Heeney and Bice are signed until the end of 2028.

Blakey is reportedly seeking a trade to Victorian rivals, but football boss Leon Cameron had dismissed those rumblings as "speculation" earlier this month.

Victoria Police's eight-week timeline prediction on their investigation into the Pullman Hotel incident - which was first flagged on September 2 - takes in the free agency and trade period from October 2 to October 14.

Main ball-winners Heeney and Warner weren't invited to Monday night's Brownlow Medal at Crown Palladium, but remained eligible for the award.

Heeney and Warner are expected to be frontrunners for Sydney's Bob Skilton Medal, to be held after Saturday's grand final.

Swans chief executive Matthew Pavlich spoke to reporters earlier on Wednesday and said the club would hear the group out.

"I want them to be themselves," Pavlich said of what he wanted to hear from the players.

"I want them to come in and do what we'd normally do at the end of a season, which is, yeah, player exit meetings.

"If they've got something to say to their player group, if they've got something to say to the club, then we'll hear them out then."
